text:
A: Hiya mate! Can you hear me? Jaspal, Derby.
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Joel, I'm in Manchester. Levenshulme.
A: Manchester, nice. I've been to the Etihad once for a cup game and we got battered, so I've got mixed feelings about the place.
B: (laughs) Don't worry, I'm Liverpool, so I've got mixed feelings about it as well. I get proper stick at work for it.
A: A Liverpool fan in Manchester? Brave man. What do you do?
B: Solicitor, corporate. Business sales mostly, share purchases. You're a teacher, I'm guessing? Gemma said there was a teacher in Derby with a dog called Biscuit.
A: Ha, the Biscuit thing's gone right round the study, hasn't it? Yeah, sixth form, Business and Economics. And the best bit is, my partner's a physio called Gemma as well. When Craig told me he'd met a physio called Gemma with a Biscuit, I genuinely had a moment.
B: Stop it. My girlfriend's a physio too! Hannah, MSK, NHS.
A: You're joking. Is everyone in this study going out with a physio?
B: Seems like it. She talks about the waiting list like it's a third person in the house.
A: Same! Gemma comes home and just goes "don't". That's the whole conversation. So corporate law, is that the all-nighters sort of thing?
B: Can be. Had a completion run till midnight Tuesday. Mostly it's fine, but when a deal's busy it's sixty hours a week, and you sort of just crack on. I try and keep Wednesday nights for five-a-side.
A: Wednesday five-a-side! That's me. Third person today that's said that, by the way. Craig does it, I do it, you do it.
B: (laughs) It's the national day for it. Are you any good?
A: Honestly? No. I'm there for the pint after. I tell people I'm a holding midfielder because I hold the one position and don't move. Do you play fantasy football?
B: Yeah, with uni mates. I'm losing, badly. Bottom three.
A: I run the one for staff at college, and I'll be honest, I'm second, and the bloke in first is the head of maths, so it's become a whole thing. He sends graphs.
B: Graphs? That's not on.
A: That's what I said! Spreadsheet warfare. Do you get out to anything in Manchester, comedy or that?
B: Frog and Bucket now and again. And gigs, Albert Hall, the Ritz. Hannah drags me to the big pop shows and I pretend I'm not enjoying it.
A: Ha, I love that. I go to the Glee Club in Nottingham, stand-up's my thing. Saw a lad there last time who did twenty minutes on Greggs and it was the best night of my life, nearly.
B: Greggs material always lands, to be fair. Where's home originally?
A: Kabul, if you go far enough back. Afghan Sikh, came over when I was nine. Derby ever since, though. You?
B: Warrington. Turns out Craig lives round the corner from my mum and dad, which was mad.
A: It's a village, this study. Right, what are you doing for holidays? Because I'm trying to talk Gemma into Benidorm with the lads and it's not going well.
B: (laughs) Benidorm's a hard sell. Mallorca with Hannah, most summers. Japan's on the list, if work ever calms down.
A: Japan, now that's a proper one. Sorry, go on, were you going to say something?
B: No, just, if it ever happens. Everyone I know says it'll calm down next year, and it never does, you know.
